scope: Source-only review of separately derived existing CVC RW phase dispatch, plus new unchanged-time regression fixtures. Not an execution pass.
checks: RW callbacks append to their existing typed callback list in registration order. A batch is detached only when pending active/inactive and NBA work has settled.
Detached events enter existing pending-event dispatch with the compiled sentinel or interpreter NULL tail; the old dispatch retains IDP, callback execution and event reclamation.
The interpreter loops through newly generated NBA work before taking another RW batch or reaching RO.
All four generated move_time variants test the RW queue before slot-end RO and before deciding whether the future event heap is empty.
The compiled jump uses existing event-entry code and pending-list cleanup. It neither changes __simtime nor adds a settling delay.
Future carriers update cbtevp to the current queued event, so cancellation no longer targets the freed carrier. Removal uses the existing cancellation entry and null callback payload.
New RW batches queued during a batch remain separate. Ordinary pending-event machinery settles changes and NBA work before the next batch.
Existing callback initialization/reset ownership is reused; no new HDL scheduler, CPU model or global simulator option is introduced.
Old clock/NBA waves sample input0 before RW writes1
Current RW batch retains first/peer order
Nested RW follows two fresh NBA waves and precedes already-registered RO
Cancellation before carrier, after carrier reaches batch, and newly queued zero-RW callback
No future HDL fallback keeps the slot alive; missing receipt is failure even on exit0
